subtopicTitle: Barrowman equations — centre of pressure calculation for finned rockets

cards.front: What are the Barrowman equations used for in rocket design?
cards.back: Semi-empirical method to compute the longitudinal center of pressure (CP) of slender, fin-stabilized rockets by superposing normal-force contributions of the body and fins.

cards.front: State the general Barrowman formula for CP location $x_{cp}$.
cards.back: $$x_{cp}=\frac{\sum_i(C_{N\alpha,i}\cdot x_i)}{\sum_i C_{N\alpha,i}}$$ where $x_i$ is the CP coordinate of component $i$ measured from the nose tip.

cards.front: What is the normal-force-curve slope $C_{N\alpha}$ of a slender axisymmetric body according to Barrowman?
cards.back: $C_{N\alpha,\text{body}}=2$ (per radian) for a pointed nose plus cylindrical body; the body CP lies at the centroid of the planform area.

cards.front: Give the Barrowman expression for $C_{N\alpha}$ of a set of $N$ identical trapezoidal fins.
Where is the CP of each fin located in the Barrowman method?
cards.back: At the quarter-chord point of the mean aerodynamic chord (MAC), measured perpendicular to the rocket axis; the MAC is found from the root and tip chord geometry.

cards.front: How does the presence of a body affect fin $C_{N\alpha}$ (Barrowman interference factor)?
cards.back: Multiply isolated-fin $C_{N\alpha}$ by the body-fin interference factor $K_{B(F)}\approx 1+\frac{r}{s+r}$ where $r$ is body radius and $s$ is semi-span; also add the opposite fin-body carry-over term.

cards.front: What is a key limitation of the Barrowman equations?
cards.back: Valid only for subsonic, incompressible flow on slender bodies (angle of attack < 10°); does not account for compressibility, viscosity, or large vortex effects at high Mach or high AoA.
